tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	"""Lean browsing: the model decides, code does the mechanics. A drop-in for `browser_agent.browse()`.
2	
3	browse() runs a browser-use agent: the model locates element indexes, drags sliders and retries clicks itself, at
4	3-5 s and one model call per click (400-550 calls per sandbox run). Here each step is: code clears the page (the
5	PopupGuard: cookie walls, notices, error pages, robot gates), turns it into compact text plus numbered elements (links
6	with their hrefs, buttons, fields, iframes and open shadow roots included), and asks the model ONE question: what to
7	do on this page. The model still chooses where to go, what to search for and what to save (fair play); code only
8	clicks, types, reads and saves what it chose.
9	
10	The reply uses the same action names as the browser-use agents, so the scrapers' job prompts stay valid:
11	{"memory": "...", "action": [{"click": {"index": 3}}, {"read_page": {"topic": "..."}}, ...]}.
12	Pages are driven with Playwright over CDP on the run's browsers (locally: one Chromium, a context per browser).
13	"""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import asyncio
17	import base64
18	import json
19	import logging
20	import os
21	import weakref
22	from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse
23	
24	import browsers
25	from swarm import timeline
26	from swarm.browser_agent import PAGE_TEXT_LIMIT, RecordParams, Tab, allowed_domains, main_tab, normalize_actions, \
27	    site_tips
28	from swarm.forms import fill_fields, scoped_evaluator
29	from swarm.guard import PopupGuard
30	from swarm.page_text import EXTRACT_JS, FRAME_MISSING, NEXT_JS, clean
31	
32	log = logging.getLogger("lean")
33	
34	MODEL_TIMEOUT_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_LEAN_MODEL_TIMEOUT_S", "45"))
35	ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000
36	ACTION_BUDGET_S = 60         # one action at most (a read of a paged list included)
37	TEXT_LIMIT = 7000            # page text shown to the model per step
38	ELEMENT_LIMIT = 180          # numbered elements shown per step (new ones first)
39	MAX_ACTIONS = 5              # actions per reply
40	ROLES = ("tender", "spec", "erp", "mail")
41	
42	SYSTEM = """You operate business websites for a sales team to do ONE job. Each turn you get the job, your notes so far,
43	the result of your last actions, and the current page: URL, title, its text and its numbered interactive elements
44	(links show their href). Cookie walls, notices, error pages and robot gates (slider + checkbox) are usually cleared
45	for you before you see the page; if one is still there, operate it yourself.
46	
47	Reply JSON only: {"memory": "1-3 short sentences: what is done, what you learned, the next goal",
48	 "action": [ {<one action>}, ... ]}  (1-5 actions, run in order; after an action that loads another page the rest
49	 are skipped, so put the page-changing action last).
50	Actions:
51	 {"click": {"index": N}}                       click element N
52	 {"input": {"index": N, "text": "..."}}        type into field N (replaces its value)
53	 {"select_dropdown": {"index": N, "text": "option label"}}
54	 {"check": {"index": N, "on": true}}           tick/untick a checkbox or radio
55	 {"slide": {"index": N}}                       drag slider N to its maximum (like a person)
56	 {"fill_form": {"fields": [{"field": "label or name", "value": "..."}], "apply_button": "", "then_click": "button text"}}
57	     several fields at once by their labels, in order; checkbox "true"/"false", slider "max". apply_button: the
58	     button that enables the next dependent select (pressed between them for you), so one fill_form sets them all
59	 {"send_keys": {"keys": "Enter"}}
60	 {"navigate": {"url": "..."}}                  only URLs/hrefs seen on this site, never invented ones
61	 {"read_page": {"topic": "short label", "url": "", "urls": [], "next_page_link": "", "evidence_role": ""}}
62	     save page text as evidence for the analysts (topic required to save). url/urls: open those hrefs from this page
63	     and save each; next_page_link: exact text of the paging link, every page is followed and saved.
64	 {"read_visual": {"topic": "what to transcribe"}}   read text drawn in an image/canvas (e.g. a code to copy)
65	 {"record": {"kind": "label", "data": {...}, "source": "", "note": ""}}   save one fact as you see it
66	 {"share_tip": {"tip": "..."}}                one short how-to for this site for other agents (URL pattern etc.)
67	 {"done": {"text": "what you found/did, with the key facts", "success": true}}
68	Rules: save (read_page with a topic) every page holding facts the job needs BEFORE done. Use the elements' hrefs
69	exactly; a guessed URL returns 404. Links that lead away from the content ("accept and continue" banners, ads,
70	downloads) are decoys. Look-alike references (suffixes like -A), drafts, superseded versions and mails from other
71	senders do not count, but note them. Be brief; do not repeat steps that worked."""
72	
73	# Runs in a frame: (offset) => elements. Numbers the visible interactive elements (open shadow roots included) and
74	# tags each with data-lean-id so a locator finds it again.
75	ELEMENTS_JS = r"""(offset) => {
76	  const norm = s => (s || '').replace(/[​-‍⁠﻿]/g, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
77	  const shown = el => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); const s = getComputedStyle(el);
78	    return (r.width > 0 || r.height > 0) && s.visibility !== 'hidden' && s.display !== 'none'; };
79	  const roots = [document];
80	  for (let i = 0; i < roots.length && i < 40; i++) for (const el of roots[i].querySelectorAll('*')) if (el.shadowRoot) roots.push(el.shadowRoot);
81	  for (const root of roots) for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('[data-lean-id]')) el.removeAttribute('data-lean-id');
82	  const sel = 'a[href], button, input:not([type=hidden]), select, textarea, summary, [role=button], [role=link], [role=tab], [role=menuitem], [role=checkbox], [role=slider], [role=option]';
83	  const out = []; let n = offset;
84	  for (const root of roots) for (const el of root.querySelectorAll(sel)) {
85	    if (out.length >= 400) break;
86	    const kind = (el.type || '').toLowerCase();
87	    if (!shown(el) && !['checkbox', 'radio', 'range'].includes(kind)) continue;
88	    el.setAttribute('data-lean-id', String(n));
89	    const tag = el.tagName.toLowerCase();
90	    const label = norm(el.getAttribute('aria-label') || (el.labels && el.labels[0] && el.labels[0].innerText) ||
91	      el.placeholder || el.title || el.innerText || (tag === 'input' ? '' : el.value) || el.name || el.id || '').slice(0, 80);
92	    const item = {id: n, tag, label};
93	    if (kind) item.type = kind;
94	    if (tag === 'a') item.href = el.getAttribute('href');
95	    if (tag === 'input' || tag === 'textarea') {
96	      if (kind === 'checkbox' || kind === 'radio') item.checked = el.checked;
97	      else item.value = norm(el.value).slice(0, 60);
98	      if (kind === 'range') { item.min = el.min || '0'; item.max = el.max || '100'; }
99	    }
100	    if (tag === 'select') { item.value = el.value; item.options = [...el.options].slice(0, 15).map(o => norm(o.text)); }
101	    if (el.disabled) item.disabled = true;
102	    out.push(item); n++;
103	  }
104	  return out;
105	}"""
106	
107	SLIDERS_JS = r"""() => [...document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]')]
108	  .filter(r => (r.offsetWidth || r.offsetHeight) && !r.disabled && Number(r.value) < Number(r.max || 100))
109	  .map(r => { r.scrollIntoView({block: 'center'}); const b = r.getBoundingClientRect();
110	              return [b.left + 3, b.right - 2, b.top + b.height / 2]; })"""
111	
112	# --- browsers and pages ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
113	
114	_PW = None
115	_LOCAL = None
116	_CONTEXTS: dict[int, object] = {}
117	# Tab -> the Playwright page it works in. Keyed by the Tab itself: id() values are reused once a worker Tab is gone,
118	# and a new Tab with a reused id inherited a page its old owner was closing (TargetClosedError in parallel ERP workers).
119	_PAGES: "weakref.WeakKeyDictionary" = weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()
120	_DIALOGS: set[int] = set()              # pages whose native dialogs are accepted
121	
122	
123	def watch_dialogs(page) -> None:
124	    """Accept native dialogs (alert, confirm such as "submit binding bid?", beforeunload): a model that clicked the
125	    button already decided; an open dialog would block the page."""
126	    if id(page) in _DIALOGS:
127	        return
128	    _DIALOGS.add(id(page))
129	
130	    async def accept(dialog):
131	        log.info("accepting %s dialog: %s", dialog.type, dialog.message[:200])
132	        try:
133	            await dialog.accept()
134	        except Exception as error:
135	            log.debug("dialog: %s", error)
136	
137	    page.on("dialog", lambda dialog: asyncio.ensure_future(accept(dialog)))
138	_LOCK = asyncio.Lock()
139	_LOGIN_LOCKS: dict[tuple, asyncio.Lock] = {}   # (browser, host) -> one tab logs in / passes the gate at a time
140	
141	# Runs in the page: () => true while it is a login or access-gate page (a password field, or a slider not at its end)
142	LOCKED_JS = r"""() => !!document.querySelector('input[type=password]') ||
143	  [...document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]')].some(r => (r.offsetWidth || r.offsetHeight) && Number(r.value) < Number(r.max || 100))"""
144	
145	
146	_INDEX_LOCKS: dict[int, asyncio.Lock] = {}
147	
148	# Search-help result links close their window (SAP-style popup). In a tab the agent opened that kills the agent's page,
149	# so window.close() only works for windows another page opened.
150	KEEP_OPEN_JS = "(() => { const close = window.close.bind(window); window.close = () => { if (window.opener) close(); }; })()"
151	
152	
153	async def _context(index: int):
154	    """Browser `index`'s context: over CDP in a run; locally one Chromium with a context per browser index.
155	    A browser that does not answer within 30 s raises (the caller falls back to another one)."""
156	    global _PW, _LOCAL
157	    async with _LOCK:
158	        if _PW is None:
159	            from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
160	            _PW = await async_playwright().start()
161	    async with _INDEX_LOCKS.setdefault(index, asyncio.Lock()):
162	        if index in _CONTEXTS:
163	            return _CONTEXTS[index]
164	        urls = browsers.cdp_urls()
165	        if urls:
166	            browser = await asyncio.wait_for(_PW.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[index % len(urls)]), 30)
167	            context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
168	        else:
169	            async with _LOCK:
170	                if _LOCAL is None:
171	                    _LOCAL = await _PW.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
172	            context = await _LOCAL.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800})
173	        try:        # a tab we opened can close itself (one history entry); only real popups may
174	            await context.add_init_script(KEEP_OPEN_JS)
175	        except Exception as error:
176	            log.debug("init script: %s", error)
177	        _CONTEXTS[index] = context
178	        return context
179	
180	
181	async def page_for(tab: Tab):
182	    """The page `tab` works in: kept across browse calls (logged in, current page), created on first use."""
183	    page = _PAGES.get(tab)
184	    if page is not None and not page.is_closed():
185	        return page
186	    count = max(1, len(browsers.cdp_urls()))
187	    context, use_main = None, tab.main
188	    for shift in range(count):                       # a browser that does not answer: the next one
189	        index = (tab.browser + shift) % count
190	        try:
191	            context = await _context(index)
192	            break
193	        except Exception as error:
194	            log.warning("browser %d not usable (%s); trying the next one", index, type(error).__name__)
195	            use_main = False
196	    if context is None:
197	        raise RuntimeError("no browser answers")
198	    if use_main and browsers.cdp_urls() and context.pages:
199	        page = context.pages[0]
200	    else:
201	        page = await asyncio.wait_for(context.new_page(), 20)
202	        if browsers.cdp_urls():         # so Tab.close() closes it like a browser-use tab
203	            try:
204	                session = await context.new_cdp_session(page)
205	                info = await session.send("Target.getTargetInfo")
206	                tab.claim(info["targetInfo"]["targetId"])
207	                await session.detach()
208	            except Exception as error:
209	                log.debug("target id: %s", error)
210	    _PAGES[tab] = page
211	    return page
212	
213	
214	# --- reading -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
215	
216	async def page_text(page) -> str:
217	    """Page text (frames, shadow roots, canvas labels); frames the page cannot see into are read in place by
218	    Playwright (it reaches cross-origin and sandboxed frames)."""
219	    text = clean(str(await page.evaluate(EXTRACT_JS, {})))
220	    if FRAME_MISSING in text:
221	        for frame in page.frames[1:]:
222	            try:
223	                inner = clean(str(await frame.evaluate(EXTRACT_JS, {})))
224	            except Exception:

245	def order_elements(items: list[dict], seen: set) -> tuple[list[dict], set]:
246	    """Elements that appeared since the last step first (an opened menu, a dialog, results), marked NEW; capped."""
247	    keys = [(e.get("tag"), e.get("label"), e.get("href")) for e in items]
248	    fresh = [e for e, k in zip(items, keys) if seen and k not in seen]
249	    for e in fresh:
250	        e["new"] = True
251	    rest = [e for e, k in zip(items, keys) if not (seen and k not in seen)]
252	    return (fresh + rest)[:ELEMENT_LIMIT], set(keys)

257	    for e in items:
258	        line = f"[{e['id']}] {e['tag']}{'/' + e['type'] if e.get('type') else ''} \"{e.get('label', '')}\""
259	        if e.get("href"):
260	            line += f" -> {e['href'][:120]}"
261	        if "value" in e and e["value"] not in ("", None):
262	            line += f" value=\"{e['value']}\""
263	        if "checked" in e:

265	        if e.get("type") == "range":

269	        if e.get("disabled"):
270	            line += " disabled"
271	        if e.get("new"):
272	            line += "  NEW"
273	        lines.append(line)

325	async def _lean(ctx, goal, *, browser, tab, site_id, on_record, max_steps, hints, author, stop_reserve, stop_extra,
326	                careful, idle_steps, stop_on_record, extra_actions) -> dict:
327	    records: list[dict] = []
328	    state = {"saved_at": None, "steps": 0}
329	    tab = tab or main_tab(browser)
330	    page = await asyncio.wait_for(page_for(tab), 75)
331	    log.info("%s: working in %s", author, page.url[:80] or "a new tab")
332	    task = ctx.task if ctx is not None else {}
333	    secrets = [str((s.get("credentials") or {}).get("password") or "") for s in (task.get("access") or [])]
334	
335	    def reserve() -> float:
336	        if stop_reserve is not None:
337	            return stop_reserve
338	        return ctx.stop_at(stop_extra) if ctx is not None and hasattr(ctx, "stop_at") else stop_extra
339	
340	    def mask(text: str) -> str:
341	        for secret in secrets:
342	            if len(secret) >= 4:
343	                text = text.replace(secret, "***")
344	        return text
345	
346	    async def emit(rec: dict) -> None:
347	        records.append(rec)
348	        state["saved_at"] = state["steps"]
349	        if on_record:
350	            await on_record(rec)
351	
352	    async def evaluate(js, *args):
353	        return await page.evaluate(js, *args)
354	
355	    async def guard_fill(pairs, then_click, item_id):
356	        await drag_sliders(page)
357	        return await fill_fields(scoped_evaluator(evaluate, item_id), pairs, "", then_click)
358	
359	    guard = PopupGuard(ctx, author, careful=careful, fill=guard_fill)
360	    tips = site_tips(ctx, site_id)
361	    hint_text = hints + ("\nTips from other agents on this site:\n- " + "\n- ".join(tips) if tips else "")
362	    if extra_actions:
363	        hint_text += "\nExtra actions for this job:\n" + "\n".join(
364	            f' {{"{name}": {{...}}}}  {help_}' for name, (help_, _) in extra_actions.items())
365	    if page.url in ("", "about:blank"):
366	        start = _first_url(goal, task, site_id)
367	        if start:
368	            try:
369	                await page.goto(start, timeout=20000, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
370	            except Exception as error:
371	                log.debug("start url: %s", error)
372	    memory: list[str] = []
373	    login_held = None
374	    seen: set = set()
375	    repeats: list[str] = []
376	    last = "Start."
377	    summary, done, success = "", False, False
378	
379	    try:
380	        for step in range(1, max_steps + 1):
381	            state["steps"] = step
382	            if ctx is not None and ctx.seconds_left() <= reserve():
383	                summary = summary or "stopped: time reserve reached"
384	                break
385	            page = _PAGES.get(tab, page)
386	            watch_dialogs(page)
387	            try:
388	                with timeline.span("guard", "sweep"):
389	                    await asyncio.wait_for(guard.sweep(evaluate), 20)
390	            except Exception as error:
391	                log.debug("guard: %s", error)
392	            # Parallel tabs on one site share the session: when several log in at once, each login ends the others'
393	            # sessions and they loop on login and gate (local run: 16 steps, nothing saved). One tab logs in at a time;
394	            # the others wait, reload, and usually find themselves logged in.
395	            try:
396	                locked = await asyncio.wait_for(page.evaluate(LOCKED_JS), 10)
397	            except Exception:
398	                locked = False
399	            key = (tab.browser, urlparse(page.url).netloc)
400	            if locked and login_held is None:
401	                lock = _LOGIN_LOCKS.setdefault(key, asyncio.Lock())
402	                if lock.locked():
403	                    try:
404	                        await asyncio.wait_for(lock.acquire(), 90)
405	                        lock.release()
406	                    except TimeoutError:
407	                        pass
408	                    try:
409	                        await page.reload(wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
410	                        locked = await asyncio.wait_for(page.evaluate(LOCKED_JS), 10)
411	                    except Exception:
412	                        pass
413	                if locked and not lock.locked():
414	                    await lock.acquire()
415	                    login_held = lock
416	            elif not locked and login_held is not None:
417	                login_held.release()
418	                login_held = None
419	            step_started = timeline.now()
420	            try:
421	                text = await asyncio.wait_for(page_text(page), 20)
422	                items, where = await asyncio.wait_for(elements(page), 20)
423	                items, seen = order_elements(items, seen)
424	                title = await asyncio.wait_for(page.title(), 10)
425	            except Exception as error:      # page navigating, hung or closed: reload, the next step reads again
426	                log.warning("%s: page not readable (%s) at %s", author, type(error).__name__, page.url[:80])
427	                last = f"page not readable ({type(error).__name__}); it was reloaded"
428	                try:
429	                    if page.is_closed():        # closed under us: a new tab on the same URL (session cookies stay)
430	                        url = page.url
431	                        _PAGES.pop(tab, None)
432	                        page = await asyncio.wait_for(page_for(tab), 30)
433	                        if url and url != "about:blank":
434	                            await page.goto(url, timeout=20000, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
435	                    else:
436	                        await page.reload(wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
437	                except Exception:
438	                    pass
439	                continue
440	            user = (f"JOB:\n{goal}\n{hint_text}\n\nYOUR NOTES SO FAR:\n" + ("\n".join(memory[-8:]) or "(none)") +
441	                    f"\n\nRESULT OF YOUR LAST ACTIONS:\n{last[:1500]}\n\nPAGE: {page.url}\nTITLE: {title}\n"
442	                    f"TEXT:\n{text[:TEXT_LIMIT]}{' …[truncated; read_page saves all of it]' if len(text) > TEXT_LIMIT else ''}"
443	                    f"\n\nELEMENTS:\n{element_lines(items)}")
444	            try:
445	                reply = await asyncio.wait_for(ctx.llm.ask_json(SYSTEM, user), MODEL_TIMEOUT_S)
446	            except Exception as error:
447	                last = f"(no reply: {type(error).__name__})"
448	                timeline.count("steps.no_reply")
449	                log.info("%s step %d: no reply (%s)", author, step, type(error).__name__)
450	                continue
451	            reply = json.loads(normalize_actions(json.dumps(reply))) if isinstance(reply, dict) else {}
452	            note = str(reply.get("memory") or "").strip()
453	            if note:
454	                memory.append(f"{step}. {note}")
455	            actions = reply.get("action") or []
456	            actions = actions if isinstance(actions, list) else [actions]
457	            results = []
458	            for action in actions[:MAX_ACTIONS]:
459	                if not isinstance(action, dict) or not action:
460	                    continue
461	                name, params = next(iter(action.items()))
462	                params = params if isinstance(params, dict) else {}
463	                before = page.url
464	                finish = False
465	                try:
466	                    if name in extra_actions:
467	                        result = await extra_actions[name][1](params, page)
468	                        result, finish = result if isinstance(result, tuple) else (result, False)
469	                        changed = False
470	                    else:
471	                        # every Playwright call here has its own timeout except page.evaluate (form filling,
472	                        # sliders): a page stuck in a script once stalled two agents for 7 minutes
473	                        result, changed = await asyncio.wait_for(
474	                            _act(name, params, page, where, ctx, site_id, author, emit, text, tab), ACTION_BUDGET_S)
475	                except Exception as error:
476	                    result, changed = f"{name} failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}", False
477	                page = _PAGES.get(tab, page)
478	                results.append(f"{name}: {result}")
479	                if finish:
480	                    done, success, summary = True, True, str(result)
481	                    break
482	                if name == "done":
483	                    done, success = True, bool(params.get("success", True))
484	                    summary = str(params.get("text") or "")
485	                    break
486	                if name == "record" and stop_on_record and params.get("kind") == stop_on_record:
487	                    done, success, summary = True, True, f"recorded {stop_on_record}"
488	                    break
489	                if changed or page.url != before:
490	                    break
491	            last = "\n".join(results) or "(no action)"
492	            signature = json.dumps(actions[:MAX_ACTIONS], sort_keys=True)[:300] + page.url
493	            repeats = (repeats + [signature])[-3:]
494	            if len(repeats) == 3 and len(set(repeats)) == 1:
495	                last += ("\nWARNING: you sent the same actions 3 times on the same page without progress. Do something "
496	                         "else (look for NEW elements, another link, read_page, or done with what you have).")
497	            timeline.add("browse.step", "step", step_started)
498	            log.info("%s step %d: %s | %s", author, step, ",".join(next(iter(a)) for a in actions[:MAX_ACTIONS]
499	                                                                     if isinstance(a, dict) and a) or "-",
500	                     mask(note)[:200])
501	            if done:
502	                break
503	            if idle_steps and state["saved_at"] is not None and step - state["saved_at"] >= idle_steps:
504	                summary = f"stopped after {idle_steps} steps without new evidence (decoy or dead end?)"
505	                timeline.count("browse.idle_stops")
506	                break
507	    finally:
508	        if login_held is not None and login_held.locked():
509	            login_held.release()
510	    tab.used = True
511	    return {"summary": summary or (memory[-1] if memory else ""), "records": records, "steps": state["steps"],
512	            "done": done and success, "finished": done, "guard_actions": guard.actions, "error": ""}

538	async def _act(name, params, page, where, ctx, site_id, author, emit, text, tab):
539	    """Run one action; returns (result for the model, page changed)."""
540	    task = ctx.task if ctx is not None else {}
541	
542	    def locate(index):
543	        frame = where.get(int(index))
544	        if frame is None:
545	            raise ValueError(f"no element {index} on this page")
546	        return frame.locator(f'[data-lean-id="{int(index)}"]').first
547	
548	    before = page.url
549	    if name == "click":
550	        context = page.context
551	        known = set(context.pages)
552	        parent = await _opener(page)            # a search-help popup closes itself and fills the window that opened it
553	        target = locate(params["index"])
554	        try:
555	            await target.click(timeout=ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS)
556	        except Exception as error:   # covered by an overlay or never "stable": the element's own click still works
557	            if "Timeout" not in type(error).__name__ and "timeout" not in str(error).lower():
558	                raise
559	            await target.evaluate("el => el.click()", timeout=ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS)
560	        await asyncio.sleep(0.4)
561	        # a tab this page opened: continue there (other agents open tabs in the same browser at the same time)
562	        opened = [p for p in context.pages if p not in known and await _opener(p) is page]
563	        if not opened and page.is_closed():     # the site moved on to a new window and closed this one
564	            await asyncio.sleep(0.6)
565	            opened = [p for p in context.pages if p not in known and not p.is_closed()]
566	            if not opened and parent is not None and not parent.is_closed():
567	                _PAGES[tab] = parent
568	                return f"this window closed; continued in the window that opened it ({parent.url})", True
569	        if opened:
570	            new = opened[-1]
571	            for _ in range(20):             # a new tab starts as about:blank before its URL loads
572	                if new.url not in ("", "about:blank"):
573	                    break
574	                await asyncio.sleep(0.25)
575	            try:
576	                await new.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=8000)
577	            except Exception:
578	                pass
579	            _PAGES[tab] = new
580	            return f"opened a new tab {new.url}", True
581	        return "clicked", await settle(page, before)
582	    if name == "input":
583	        await locate(params["index"]).fill(str(params.get("text", "")), timeout=ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS)
584	        return "typed", False
585	    if name == "select_dropdown":
586	        target = locate(params["index"])
587	        label = str(params.get("text", ""))
588	        try:
589	            await target.select_option(label=label, timeout=ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS)
590	        except Exception:
591	            await target.select_option(value=label, timeout=ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS)
592	        return "selected", await settle(page, before)
593	    if name == "check":
594	        await locate(params["index"]).set_checked(bool(params.get("on", True)), timeout=ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS)
595	        return "set", False
596	    if name == "slide":
597	        box = await locate(params["index"]).bounding_box()
598	        if box:
599	            y = box["y"] + box["height"] / 2
600	            await page.mouse.move(box["x"] + 3, y)
601	            await page.mouse.down()
602	            await page.mouse.move(box["x"] + box["width"] - 2, y, steps=10)
603	            await page.mouse.up()
604	        return "dragged to the end", False
605	    if name == "fill_form":
606	        pairs = [(str(f.get("field", "")), str(f.get("value", ""))) for f in params.get("fields") or []
607	                 if isinstance(f, dict)]
608	        if any(v.strip().lower() == "max" for _, v in pairs):
609	            await drag_sliders(page)
610	        report = await fill_fields(lambda js, *a: page.evaluate(js, *a), pairs, str(params.get("apply_button") or ""),
611	                                   str(params.get("then_click") or ""))
612	        return report[:400], await settle(page, before)
613	    if name == "send_keys":
614	        await page.keyboard.press(str(params.get("keys") or "Enter"))
615	        return "sent", await settle(page, before)
616	    if name == "navigate":
617	        url = _same_site(str(params.get("url", "")), page.url, task)
618	        if not url:
619	            return "refused: not a URL of this site", False
620	        response = await page.goto(url, timeout=20000, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
621	        status = response.status if response else "?"
622	        return f"opened ({status})", True
623	    if name == "read_page":       # only a read that opened other pages changes what the model sees
624	        moved = bool(params.get("url") or params.get("urls") or params.get("next_page_link"))
625	        return await _read(params, page, ctx, site_id, author, emit, tab), moved
626	    if name == "read_visual":
627	        return await _visual(params, page, ctx, site_id, author, emit), False
628	    if name == "record":
629	        record = RecordParams.model_validate(params)
630	        data = dict(record.data)
631	        data["_observed_text"] = text[:6000]
632	        await emit({"kind": record.kind, "data": data, "source": record.source or page.url, "note": record.note,
633	                    "site": site_id, "author": author})
634	        return f"recorded {record.kind}", False
635	    if name == "share_tip":
636	        tip = str(params.get("tip") or "").strip()
637	        if ctx is not None and tip:
638	            tips = dict(ctx.board.get("tips") or {})
639	            have = tips.get(site_id) or []
640	            if tip not in have and len(have) < 6:
641	                tips[site_id] = have + [tip[:300]]
642	                await ctx.board.set("tips", tips)
643	        return "tip shared", False
644	    if name == "done":
645	        return "done", False
646	    return f"unknown action {name!r}", False

649	async def _read(params, page, ctx, site_id, author, emit, tab) -> str:
650	    """read_page: save the current page (or the given hrefs, or every page of a paged list) as evidence."""
651	    task = ctx.task if ctx is not None else {}
652	    topic = str(params.get("topic") or "")
653	    role = str(params.get("evidence_role") or "")
654	    kind = f"{role}.page" if role in ROLES else "page"
655	    targets = [u for u in ([params.get("url")] + list(params.get("urls") or [])) if u]
656	    out = []
657	
658	    async def keep(text: str, number: int) -> None:
659	        if topic:
660	            await emit({"kind": kind, "data": {"topic": topic, "url": page.url, "title": await page.title(),
661	                                               "pages": 1, "page_in_read": number, "text": text},
662	                        "source": page.url, "note": "", "site": site_id, "author": author})
663	
664	    for target in targets or [None]:
665	        if target:
666	            url = _same_site(str(target), page.url, task)
667	            if not url:
668	                out.append(f"{target}: refused (not this site)")
669	                continue
670	            response = await page.goto(url, timeout=20000, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
671	            await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
672	            if response is not None and response.status >= 400:
673	                out.append(f"{target}: HTTP {response.status} (wrong URL: use the hrefs shown)")
674	                continue
675	        pages = [await page_text(page)]
676	        await keep(pages[0], 1)
677	        link = str(params.get("next_page_link") or "")
678	        while link and len(pages) < 20:
679	            if await page.evaluate(NEXT_JS, link) != "clicked":
680	                break
681	            text = pages[-1]
682	            for _ in range(12):
683	                await asyncio.sleep(0.4)
684	                text = await page_text(page)
685	                if text != pages[-1]:
686	                    break
687	            if text in pages:
688	                break
689	            pages.append(text)
690	            await keep(text, len(pages))
691	        share = max(1500, 9000 // max(1, len(pages) * len(targets or [None])))
692	        joined = "\n----- next page -----\n".join(p[:share] for p in pages)
693	        out.append(f"=== {page.url} ({len(pages)} page(s){', saved as ' + repr(topic) if topic else ''})\n{joined}")
694	    return "\n".join(out)[:12000]

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Save a run's full log locally as Markdown, so it can be read and searched without waiting for the platform.

  Writes .swarm/runs/<run>-log.md (whole log, replaced on every pull) and adds a line to .swarm/runs/<run>.md (notes:
  status, scores and MCP results go there). .swarm/ is git-ignored and never packaged: run logs hold scenario
  values, which must never get into the package.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\pull-run.ps1 run_415bcaed321664dc            # once (run ended or a snapshot)
  .\scripts\pull-run.ps1 run_415bcaed321664dc -Follow    # keep writing until the run ends

  From Git Bash / a Claude Code Monitor:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/pull-run.ps1 <run> -Follow
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$RunId,
    [switch]$Follow
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)
$dir = ".swarm/runs"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dir | Out-Null
$notes = "$dir/$RunId.md"
$logFile = "$dir/$RunId-log.md"
$now = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm 'UTC'")

# cmd merges stderr (atira writes progress there) without PowerShell 5.1 turning each line into an error record
$status = (cmd /c "atira status 2>&1" | Select-String -SimpleMatch $RunId | Select-Object -First 1)
$status = if ($status) { $status.Line.Trim() } else { "(not in atira status)" }

if (-not (Test-Path $notes)) {
    Set-Content -Encoding utf8 $notes "# $RunId`n`nFull log: [$RunId-log.md]($RunId-log.md). Notes and MCP pulls below, newest last.`n"
}
Add-Content -Encoding utf8 $notes "`n## $now - log pulled`n`nStatus: $status`n"

# The platform keeps only the tail of a long log: a later pull can hold FEWER early lines than an earlier one. So the
# file is never replaced: lines it does not have yet are appended (in the order the platform returns them).
$known = New-Object 'System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]'

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Save a run's full log locally as Markdown, so it can be read and searched without waiting for the platform.

  Writes .swarm/runs/<run>-log.md (whole log, replaced on every pull) and adds a line to .swarm/runs/<run>.md (notes:
  status, scores and MCP results go there). .swarm/ is git-ignored and never packaged: run logs hold scenario
  values, which must never get into the package.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\pull-run.ps1 run_415bcaed321664dc            # once (run ended or a snapshot)
  .\scripts\pull-run.ps1 run_415bcaed321664dc -Follow    # keep writing until the run ends

  From Git Bash / a Claude Code Monitor:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/pull-run.ps1 <run> -Follow
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$RunId,
    [switch]$Follow
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)
$dir = ".swarm/runs"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dir | Out-Null
$notes = "$dir/$RunId.md"
$logFile = "$dir/$RunId-log.md"
$now = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm 'UTC'")

# cmd merges stderr (atira writes progress there) without PowerShell 5.1 turning each line into an error record
$status = (cmd /c "atira status 2>&1" | Select-String -SimpleMatch $RunId | Select-Object -First 1)
$status = if ($status) { $status.Line.Trim() } else { "(not in atira status)" }

if (-not (Test-Path $notes)) {
    Set-Content -Encoding utf8 $notes "# $RunId`n`nFull log: [$RunId-log.md]($RunId-log.md). Notes and MCP pulls below, newest last.`n"
}
Add-Content -Encoding utf8 $notes "`n## $now - log pulled`n`nStatus: $status`n"

# The platform keeps only the tail of a long log: a later pull can hold FEWER early lines than an earlier one. So the
# file is never replaced: lines it does not have yet are appended (in the order the platform returns them).
$known = New-Object 'System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]'
if (Test-Path $logFile) {

A record opens only by clicking its row in the F4 list; direct /material/<no> URLs return 404. Prices and stock are almost never read.

**Why:** these points decide quality now; speed is already good (collection takes 8â€“10 min).

Commit with the PowerShell tool (`Start-Process git commit -F <file>` with a WaitForExit guard), never from the Bash tool.

**Why:** On 2026-10-10 `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg` hung with no output whenever started from Claude Code's Git Bash (even run by hand with stdin from /dev/null). The same hook finished in a few seconds from PowerShell and added the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer. Stuck hooks pile up: one from an earlier commit had been hanging for 3.5 h. The user wants every commit linked to Entire ("attach entire"), so `--no-verify` is not an option.

**How to apply:** Before committing, check for leftover `prepare-commit-msg` processes (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process) and end them. After committing, confirm with `git log -1 --format='%(trailers)'` that the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is present.

Run unit tests as `uv run --isolated --python 3.12 --with pytest python -m pytest tests -q` before starting a sandbox test run.

description: "What test runs on 2026-10-10 showed about where the swarm loses data (ERP, matcher, mail duplication, logs)"
metadata:

---

Test runs on 2026-10-10 (run_d1ee, run_e058, run_9643) all scored quality 10: decision and reference were right, and every position was omitted.

- **ERP item browses run out of 30 steps.** Each one spends its steps on login checks, the maintenance dialog, "Dienst vorÃ¼bergehend nicht verfÃ¼gbar", MM03 and the F4 search. A record opens only by clicking its row in the F4 list; direct /material/<no> URLs return 404. Prices and stock are almost never read.
- **The matcher drops candidates that were collected.** The F4 list has no certification, so an empty value counts as a mismatch. A requirement given as usable stroke needs the mail's reserve value, and without it nothing matches. With zero materials, BidCalculator returned no_bid (run_9643).
- **Collection ends too early.** The swarm leaves COLLECT about 8â€“10 min in, with lots of time left, because the agent's "done" counts as success even when its summary says data is missing.
- **Mail tabs read the same messages.** Each tab searches "<ref> <topic>", logs in again and passes the slider gate again.
- **The platform log keeps only the last ~2â€“3 min.** The verbose browser_use output (pydantic validation dumps) pushes out the analyst lines.
- **Flash-mode validation error.** The model puts two actions in one object, e.g. {"record":â€¦, "click":â€¦}.

**Why:** these points decide quality now; speed is already good (collection takes 8â€“10 min).
**How to apply:** fix the ERP flow (search-list stage, then per-material stage), make the matcher tolerate unknown fields, add gap-driven follow-up browses, dedupe mail reads, and reduce log noise. See [[atira-cli-path]].

Author: CRUBSTERINO <vperepelytsyn@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Oct 11 06:29:32 2026 +0200

    Tab scheduler: parallel jobs run on whichever browser has room
    
    Every site used to own one browser; tender and spec finished early and two browsers sat idle while eight ERP
    tabs shared one. swarm/scheduler.py leases tabs on the least loaded browser (4 browses per browser, a browser
    already logged in to the site preferred, one login per browser and site at a time, released tabs pooled and
    reused). ERP jobs, mail topic tabs, the Q&A tab and coordinator follow-ups use it; ERP pre-warms two tabs and
    reads prices/stock of the first candidates next to their record. Sandbox run reh_def25b3b6ab5ef06: q 96.1 in
    10:06 (was 18:42 at the same quality).
    
    Also: never close a browser's last page (Chrome quits with it), page scripts bounded to 15 s, a tab keeps its
    browser session between browses (SWARM_REUSE_SESSIONS), get_signing_tan checks the summary itself, the TAN
    lookup clears a search via the URL, startup milestones and browse.connect spans, commitment material described
    in the mail extraction shape, local-run logging that tolerates a reader.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+def _exit_now(code: int) -> None:
+    """Leave without waiting for leftover tasks, threads or browser connections: run reh_3d75a2747df66520 logged

+def _deadline_watchdog(task: dict) -> None:
+    """A thread that ends the process once the run has expired, whatever the event loop is doing."""
+    left = contract.seconds_left(task)

+        timer = threading.Timer(max(left + 5, 1), lambda: (print("run expired: exiting", flush=True), _exit_now(1)))
+        timer.daemon = True
+        timer.start()
+

"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import run as contract
from swarm.orchestrator import run_swarm


async def solve(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool) -> dict | None:
    """Runs the swarm (see docs/SWARM.md). Agents live in agents/; the orchestrator runs them phase by phase.

    For an "api" submission the swarm leaves the answer in board.results["answer"]; for a "site" submission the
    submit agent enters it on the website and the result is None.
    """
    return await run_swarm(task, playwright, scored)


async def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    try:
        async with async_playwright() as playwright:
            answer = await solve(task, playwright, scored=bool(token))
    except Exception as error:
        logging.getLogger("agent").error("Workflow failed: %s", error)
        return 1
    if answer is None:
        print("Portal submission confirmed; no API answer to post"
              if task["submission"].get("kind") == "site" else "No answer to submit", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


async def _main_then_exit() -> int:
    """main(), then a hard exit within 10 s: leftover tasks (guard loops, a pending TAN lookup, browser sessions) kept
    asyncio.run() from returning after the workflow had ended, so the run stayed 'running' until the platform's
    timeout (run_2746dd8a30f278e2: still running 10 min after 'Workflow failed')."""
    import os
    import threading
    code = await main()
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        stream.flush()
    timer = threading.Timer(10, os._exit, [code])
    timer.daemon = True
    timer.start()
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(_main_then_exit()))

class TanParams(BaseModel):
    new_request: bool = Field(default=False, description="True only after explicitly requesting a replacement TAN in the portal")
    requested_at: str = Field(default="", description="when you requested the TAN (as shown), if known")


class ReceiptParams(BaseModel):

    reference: str = Field(description="Tender reference for this receipt")


def bid_table(bid: dict, tender: dict) -> str:
    lines = []
    answer = bid.get("answer") or {}
    by_pos = {e["position"]: e for e in answer.get("positions") or []}
    for line in bid.get("lines") or []:
        pos = line["position"]
        if pos not in by_pos:
            lines.append(f"- Position {pos}: OMIT this position (use the omit/skip option for it).")
            continue
        e, disp = by_pos[pos], line.get("display") or {}
        req = {k: v for k, v in (line.get("configuration") or {}).items() if v} or line.get("required") or {}
        extra = ", ".join(f"{label} {disp[k]}" for k, label in (("base_unit_price", "base price per piece before discount"),
                                                                  ("surcharge_per_unit", "surcharges per piece"),
                                                                  ("packaging_per_unit", "packaging per piece"),
                                                                  ("rebate_total", "project bonus for the whole position"))
                          if k in disp)
        lines.append(f"- Position {pos}: configuration bore {req.get('bore')}, stroke {req.get('stroke')}, mounting "
                     f"{req.get('mounting')}, certification {req.get('certification')} -> material {e['material_number']}; "
                     f"quantity {e['quantity']} pieces; net unit price {disp.get('unit_price')} EUR; lead time "
                     f"{e['lead_time_weeks']} weeks; breakdown (optional fields): {extra or 'leave empty'}")
    known = {line["position"] for line in bid.get("lines") or []}
    for p in (tender or {}).get("positions") or []:
        if str(p.get("position")) not in known:
            lines.append(f"- Position {p.get('position')}: OMIT this position.")
    return "\n".join(lines) or "- (no position data: omit every position the form shows)"

async def browse_until_done(self, job: str, attempts: int = 3, **kwargs) -> dict:
        """browse(); if the agent stopped without finishing (errors, step limit, a crashed browser agent), start again
        with a note on what is already saved, while time allows. Saved pages are never collected twice."""
        out = {"summary": "", "done": False}
        records = []
        for attempt in range(attempts):
            note = ""
            if attempt:
                saved = sorted({e.data.get("topic") for e in self.ctx.board.query(f"{self.role}.page")} - {None})
                note = (f"\n\nNOTE: previous attempt stopped early ({out['summary'][:300]!r}). Already saved: "
                        f"{saved or 'nothing'}. Do only what is missing.")
                timeline.count("browse.retries")
            try:
                out = await self.browse(job + note, **kwargs)
            except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - a failed connection is one failed attempt, not the end
                self.ctx.board.error(self.name, f"browse attempt {attempt + 1}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
                self.log.warning("browse attempt %d failed: %s", attempt + 1, error)
                out = {"summary": f"failed: {type(error).__name__}", "done": False, "records": [], "steps": 0}
            records.extend(out.get("records") or [])
            rejected = self.ctx.shared.get("site_invalidations", {}).get(self.role, set())
            if self.site_id in rejected:
                self.site_id = await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
                # A reused tab may still show the old application; runtime model navigates the newly assigned URL.
                job += "\nThe prior site assignment was contradicted. Navigate to the newly assigned site URL in Login."
                out["done"] = False
            if out["done"] or not self.time_for_retry(kwargs):
                break
        return {**out, "records": records}

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: submitter   NEEDS: results["bid"], results["brief"]   WRITES: enters the bid on the tender portal, signs
"""Enters the computed bid in the tender portal's submission wizard and signs it with the TAN from the webmail.

The model drives the wizard (browser 0) from the brief's submission instructions and a table of the values to enter;
`fill_form` sets many fields per step. When the wizard asks for the signing TAN the model calls `get_signing_tan`,
which runs a short browse on the mail browser (3) to read the newest TAN mail. Runs even if earlier phases failed:
then every position without data is omitted ("partial submission"), the bid is still signed.

Time savers (the submission reserve shrinks with them, see swarm.context.submit_reserve):
- WizardPrep: near the end of collection the tender portal's main tab logs in and opens the bid wizard (entering
  nothing), so the submitter starts at the wizard's first step.
- At submit start the mail browser's main tab logs in and opens the inbox, so the TAN lookup only opens the newest mail.
- check_entries compares the summary page with the values to enter in code (one step instead of re-reading pages).
"""
import os
import time
from decimal import Decimal
from swarm.normalize import de_number, norm_ref
import asyncio

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from swarm import Agent, Phase, register, timeline
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import ActionResult, browse, read_current_page, BrowserSession
from swarm.lean import lean_browse, page_text
from swarm.scraper import LEAN
from swarm.context import FINAL_MARGIN_S
from swarm.extract import brief_section
from swarm.sites import site_for

run_browse = lean_browse if LEAN else browse
TAN_WAIT_S = 25 if LEAN else 3    # lean steps are cheap: wait for the lookup instead of a poll per step

PREP_LEAD_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_PREP_LEAD_S", 150))   # warm the wizard up this long before collection ends


class CheckParams(BaseModel):
    note: str = Field(default="", description="optional: which page/step this is (e.g. summary)")


def expected_values(bid: dict) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """What the portal's summary should show, per position (material, quantity, unit price) and for the bid."""
    answer = bid.get("answer") or {}
    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    lines = {l["position"]: l for l in bid.get("lines") or []}
    for e in answer.get("positions") or []:
        disp = (lines.get(e["position"]) or {}).get("display") or {}
        out[e["position"]] = [str(e["material_number"]), str(e["quantity"]),
                              disp.get("unit_price") or de_number(Decimal(str(e["unit_price"])))]
    if answer.get("positions"):
        out["total"] = [bid.get("total_display") or de_number(Decimal(str(answer.get("total_net") or 0)))]
    return out


def check_page(text: str, expected: dict[str, list[str]]) -> list[str]:
    """Expected values not found on the page (numbers compared without spaces; case-insensitive)."""
    flat = norm_ref(text)

async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            facts, _ = await asyncio.gather(self.wait_brief(), self.login())
            facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or facts
            topics, _, _ = self.topics(facts)
            lanes = [topics[i::TOPIC_TABS + 1] for i in range(min(TOPIC_TABS + 1, len(topics)))]
            self.log.info("mail topic lanes: %s", lanes)

            async def core_done() -> None:
                await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)

            async def in_tab(group: list[str]) -> None:
                tab = Tab(self.browser)
                try:
                    await self.lane(group, facts, tab=tab)
                except Exception as error:
                    self.ctx.board.error(self.name, f"mail tab lane failed: {error}")
                finally:
                    await tab.close()

            await asyncio.gather(self.lane(lanes[0] if lanes else [], facts, first=core_done),
                                 *(in_tab(g) for g in lanes[1:]))
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)
            missing = [t for t in topics if t not in self.covered(await publish(self.ctx))]
            if missing and self.ctx.time_left() > 120:
                self.log.info("topics without a valid message after the searches: %s", missing)
                out = await self.browse_until_done(INDEX_JOB.format(missing=missing), attempts=1, max_steps=16)
                await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail", True)

async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            while True:
                ready = self.settled()
                if self.ctx.time_left() > ROUND_MIN_S:
                    gaps = [g for g in find_gaps(self.ctx.board, ready, self.saved_topics()) if g["id"] not in self.tried and self.attempts.get(g["id"], 0) < 2]
                    # a site with follow-ups running still takes new, different gaps while it has a free slot
                    busy = {r: list(self.running.values()).count(r) for r in set(self.running.values())}
                    gaps = [g for g in gaps if busy.get(g["role"], 0) < MAX_RUNNING_PER_ROLE]
                    offer = frozenset(g["id"] for g in gaps)
                    if gaps and offer == self.last_offer and self.ctx.elapsed() - self.last_plan_at < REPLAN_S:
                        gaps = []                 # the same gaps were just planned (model skipped them): not again yet
                    if gaps:
                        self.last_offer, self.last_plan_at = offer, self.ctx.elapsed()
                        self.log.info("gaps: %s", [g["id"] for g in gaps])
                        try:
                            jobs = await asyncio.wait_for(self.plan(gaps), PLAN_S)
                        except (Exception, asyncio.TimeoutError) as error:
                            self.log.warning("planning failed (%s): jobs straight from the gaps",
                                             type(error).__name__)
                            jobs = direct_jobs(gaps)
                        for job in jobs:
                            if busy.get(job["role"], 0) >= MAX_RUNNING_PER_ROLE:
                                continue                  # its gaps stay open for the next round
                            busy[job["role"]] = busy.get(job["role"], 0) + 1
                            for gid in job["gaps"]:
                                self.attempts[gid] = self.attempts.get(gid, 0) + 1
                            self.tried.update(job["gaps"])
                            task = asyncio.create_task(self.work(job))
                            self.running[task] = job["role"]
                            task.add_done_callback(lambda t: self.running.pop(t, None))
                all_done = self.settled() == set(READY)
                if self.running:
                    await asyncio.wait(list(self.running), timeout=5)
                    continue
                pending = [g for g in find_gaps(self.ctx.board, ready, self.saved_topics())
                           if g["id"] not in self.tried and self.attempts.get(g["id"], 0) < 2]
                if (all_done and not pending) or self.ctx.time_left() <= ROUND_MIN_S:
                    gaps = find_gaps(self.ctx.board, set(READY), self.saved_topics())
                    await self.ctx.board.set("gaps", gaps)
                    self.log.info("collect complete; open gaps: %s", [g["id"] for g in gaps])
                    return
                await asyncio.sleep(5)
        finally:
            tasks = list(self.running)
            for task in tasks:
                task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
